draft.title: What managers do
card: Managers get work done through other people so the business can meet its goals. They do this through four linked roles.
Planning
setting goals and deciding how to reach them.
Organising
arranging people, resources and tasks so the plan can be carried out.
Leading
guiding and motivating staff to do the work. Controlling means checking results against the goals and fixing any gaps.
draft.remember: Plan, organise, lead and control: each role feeds into the next.

a.q: A manager compares this month's sales with the target and finds sales are lower. Which role is she using?
a.why: She is checking results against a goal, which is controlling. Planning is tempting because a target is involved, but the target was set earlier. Here she is measuring results against it.
a.clue: She is comparing results with a goal.

b.q: Sam manages a bakery in Orange. He sets a goal to sell 20% more bread, then rosters extra bakers for the early shift. Which pair of roles has he used?
b.why: Setting the sales goal is planning. Rostering extra bakers arranges people and tasks to carry out the plan, which is organising. He has not yet guided staff or checked results.
b.clue: First he sets a goal, then he arranges people to achieve it.

proposal.title: What managers do
card: Planning
setting goals for the business and deciding how to reach them. It gives the other roles their direction.
Organising
arranging people, resources and tasks so the plan can be carried out.
Leading
guiding and motivating staff so they do the work and work towards the goals.
Controlling
checking results against the goals and fixing any gaps. What it finds can change plans, staffing or leadership, so all four roles link to each other.
proposal.remember: Managers plan, organise, lead and control, and the four roles link together so the business meets its goals.

a.q: A manager compares this month's sales with the target and finds sales are lower. Which role is she using?
a.why: She is measuring actual results against a goal, which is controlling. Planning is tempting because a target is involved, but the target was set earlier. Here she is checking performance against it.
a.clue: The target already exists. What is she doing with it?

b.q: Sam manages a bakery in Orange. He sets a goal to sell 20% more bread, then rosters extra bakers for the early shift. Which pair of roles has he used?
b.why: Setting the sales goal is planning. Rostering extra bakers arranges people and tasks to carry out the plan, which is organising. Leading is tempting because staff are involved, but he has not yet guided or motivated them.
b.clue: Match each of Sam's two actions to a role on its own.
